newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican capo may have been murdered - report.
newsitem.headline: Mexican capo may have been murdered - report.

text.p: Mexican drug lord Amado Carrillo Fuentes may have been murdered by one of his bodyguards instead of dying from a botched plastic surgery operation, television network Televisa said on Wednesday.

Televisa said it spoke to an unnamed source at a private Mexico City hospital where officials believe Carrillo, Mexico's most wanted drug trafficker, died after eight hours of surgery last Thursday to alter his appearance.
During its nightly newscast, Televisa said its source claimed the surgery was a complete success and that it was unlikely Carrillo, 42, died from a heart attack overnight during his recovery.
The source was quoted as saying Carrillo may have been killed by one of his bodyguards through deadly injection or an "almohadazo", the Spanish word for suffocating a victim with a pillow.
Mexican and U.S. officials have said a man calling himself Victor Flores Montes, whom they believe was actually the drug lord, died from a heart attack after surgery.
Although fingerprints from the corpse match those of Carrillo, final proof of the corpse's identity was expected shortly from a DNA test, Mexican Attorney General Jorge Madrazo said on Wednesday.
The source told Televisa that Carrillo rented out the entire fourth floor and a maternity wing of the Santa Monica hospital in the posh Mexico City neighbourhood of Polanco.

Carrillo's bodyguards had blanketed the building and were guarding his room when he died, the source told Televisa. Officials have said a doctor found the man they believe was Carrillo dead the next morning.

Three doctors performed the surgery along with two anaesthesiologists, the source said. One doctor, a Brazilian, had fled to Brazil and the two others had asked the Attorney General's Office for protection, fearing for their lives.
The report was the latest twist in a bizarre saga of how Mexico's leading drug trafficker, a billionaire and a playboy, probably met his end in a maternity hospital.
Amid rumours of the kingpin's death, the corpse was flown to his home state of Sinaloa on Saturday where his grieving mother confirmed the death to reporters.

Mexican officials, not sure of the corpse's identity, seized the body at a funeral home in Sinaloa and brought it back to Mexico City for tests. The disfigured body was exhibited on Tuesday to Mexican photographers.
